text.p: Following are highlights of the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
VJESNIK
- Subpoena has absolutely no effect since The Hague tribunal has no power to punish states, Foreign Minister Mate Granic tells a parliament's Foreign Policy Council meeting to discuss the issue.
- Electricity board (HEP) and U.S. Enron might soon strike a $1.5 billion deal to build a thermoelectric plant in Jertovec near Zagreb.
- Public sector wage rise 10 percent from July.
- William Walker to take over from General Jacques Klein as Transitional Administrator for Eastern Slavonia on August 12.

- Soccer: Today's match between Croatia Zagreb and Partizan Belgrade is a test for the whole country to behave according to European standards. Some 1,000 policemen will secure Zagreb's Maksimir stadium and another 1,000 will be on standby around the town.
- This is the most important match in our entire careers, Croatia Zagreb players say.
- Tourism: Almost three million overnights by foreigners recorded on Croatia's coast so far.

- When asked to describe this season most tourist workers say: There are many tourists, but they are spending very little. Everybody is waiting for August when better-off holiday makers usually arrive.
VECERNJI LIST

- Return of refugees will be a slow process, but there are estimates some 10,000 refugees -- Croats and Serbs -- will go back home to Eastern Slavonia and other parts of Croatia by September, says UNTAES spokesman Phil Arnold.

- Croatia will do everything to persuade Croat war crimes suspects to surrender to the The Hague tribunal if they are guaranteed a speedy trial, says deputy Defence Minister Kresimir Cosic on a visit to Washington.
- "I am not thinking of resigning," says Tourism Minister Niko Bulic after the media discovered his wife won a 12,000 kuna prize for a new tourist slogan - "Croatia paradise on earth".
- Food imports more expensive since the government raised customs levies to protect domestic production. Grocers quietly increased their margins on Croatian food items, boosting those prices as well.
- The central bank made a 77.8 million kuna profit in 1996 which was passed to the state budget.
- Interest rates declining, but are still too high for most enterprises.
- City Trust research centre forecasts economic growth at a rate of 4.5 percent this year, with industry growing 4.0 percent and tourism 20 percent. Inflation seen as hovering around 4.0 percent.
- Commentary: After the film festival in Pula even skeptics must admit that Croatian film industry is improving each year, although the progress is taking place at a snail's pace.
SLOBODNA DALMACIJA

- Devastating fire swallows more than 2,500 hectares of forest on the Adriatic island of Hvar, one of Croatia's most favourite holiday destinations. Flames threatened the resort town of Stari Grad, where alert was sounded on Tuesday.

- Nikola Kostrencic, a Croat, listed as one of the owners of Swiss bank accounts dating from the Holocaust-era. His nephew and heir Vladimir Kostrencic maintains his uncle deposited the money in 1932.
- Some 650,000 Italian tourists expected to holiday in Croatia in August. For the moment, every fourth tourist on the coast is a Czech.
- State telecoms firm HPT invested half of its average on billion German marks annual income each year between 1990 and 1996. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
